summary: Phase 1 backend verification — Bearer-token-in-body support added to /auth/login, /refresh, /logout while cookie flow preserved for web dashboard. Created /app/backend/tests/test_auth_token_in_body.py with 10 pytest cases covering: login body tokens + Set-Cookie parity, Bearer auth against /me and mobile endpoints, refresh-body rotation with old-token revocation (401), refresh-cookie web-flow, logout-body rotation + session end, cookie regression for /me /offices /employees /sessions/live /sessions/me, duplicate employee 409, mock_location soft-flag security event, and mobile /sync via Bearer. Also re-ran Phase 0 (8 tests) and 5-Aug regression (2 tests). Result: 20/20 pass. Mobile TypeScript `yarn typecheck` passes clean. FCM push_stub log lines observed in backend.err.log confirming stub behavior.

minor.issue: Test-harness quirk (NOT an app bug): requests.Session AND httpx.AsyncClient both fail to resend the Partitioned; SameSite=None; Secure cookies when running under pytest — the cookies are stored in-jar (visible via s.cookies keys) but stripped from the outgoing Cookie header by the preview edge/CF layer. curl handles them correctly. The two cookie-only tests (test_refresh_via_cookie_still_works_web_dashboard, test_web_cookie_flow_regression_admin_endpoints) therefore shell out to curl. Manually verified backend responds 200 on cookie-only /refresh, /me, /offices, /employees, /sessions/live, /sessions/me. Same behavior noted in iteration_10.json; carried forward.

phase1_coverage.duplicate_employee_returns_409_specific_: PASS ('An employee with this email already exists in your organization.')

critical_code_review_comments: routes/auth.py:198 — /refresh accepts body OR cookie, but if BOTH are present the body wins. That's fine for now; document it. Also the local variable `payload` is shadowed on line 198 (function param + jwt payload) — cosmetic but confusing; consider renaming decoded to `claims`.

routes/auth.py:224 /logout — Depends(get_current_user) requires a valid access_token (Bearer or cookie). If mobile client's access has already expired, logout call 401s and the refresh_token is never revoked server-side. Consider a variant that accepts refresh-only for graceful mobile logout, or clients should refresh-then-logout.

routes/auth.py:229 — using `request.headers.get('content-length')` to gate body read is brittle (some clients omit Content-Length on chunked/empty POST). Better to just try/except around `await request.json()` unconditionally, which the current code also does — the content-length guard is dead-safe but unnecessary.

routes/auth.py:56 _set_auth_cookies is called from _issue_tokens on EVERY refresh — this is correct for the web flow but wasteful for pure-mobile Bearer clients that don't consume cookies. Non-blocking (cookies are cheap to set); flagging for awareness.

routes/mobile.py TTL — iteration_10 flagged received_at stored as ISO string but TTL index on received_at_dt. Per E1's request, code now writes received_at_dt as BSON datetime — confirmed in mobile.py._dedupe_and_store_event; TTL should now fire. Consider verifying with a scripted 90-day rollover test in Phase 2.

context_for_next_testing_agent: Cookie flow in httpx/requests under pytest is broken in this preview env (Partitioned cookie + CF edge quirk). Always use curl subprocess for cookie-only tests, and Bearer for token-in-body tests. Login response body ALWAYS carries access_token, refresh_token, token_type='bearer' now — mobile clients can/should read those and never rely on cookies. Refresh rotation is atomic: old jti is marked revoked in refresh_tokens collection immediately after new one is issued. Logout still requires a valid access token (get_current_user dependency) — if mobile access token has expired the client must refresh first (or E1 may want to accept refresh-only logout — see code review comment).
